claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the 'Provider support policy' page linked from the support index card).
The Provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.

The Provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ describes which Pulumi providers get long-term security updates (implying some providers receive long-term security updates and others do not).
Pulumi maintains each provider major version for a defined period of time, and only certain providers receive long-term security updates.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update if an error or failure occurs.
When an error or failure occurs during an update, Pulumi completes any pending operations currently in progress and then exits and reports the error.
To manually roll back after a failed deployment, reverting the code and configuration changes and running `pulumi up` returns infrastructure to its previous state.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`; it compares the desired state in the program against the last recorded state.

Pulumi does not refresh automatically before every update because refreshing requires a round-trip to the cloud provider for every resource in a stack, adding significant latency for large stacks; this is an intentional design decision.
Running `pulumi refresh` synchronizes Pulumi's recorded state with the actual state of cloud resources.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.

The Pulumi logical name is part of the auto-assigned resource URN and only needs to be unique within a stack, while the physical name typically needs to be unique within a certain scope (sometimes globally).
Pulumi auto-naming creates each resource's physical name by combining the logical name with a random suffix appended afterwards.
Pulumi auto-naming allows Pulumi to replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement before deleting the old resource.
Auto-naming can be disabled on a per-resource basis in Pulumi.
Project or stack configuration can be used to customize or disable auto-naming globally, per provider, or per resource type.
During an update, Pulumi secrets are decrypted in memory and visible to the Pulumi program.
Passing `--secret` to `pulumi config set` encrypts the value so it can be safely persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
For every stack, Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key used to encrypt secrets for that stack, and this is configurable to use a custom secrets provider.

Because a different key is used per stack, encrypting the same value across two stacks produces different encrypted strings, so an encrypted value cannot be copied between stack config files with a text editor and `pulumi config set` must be used.
When running a preview, update or destroy, Pulumi decrypts secret data, which is plain text during execution and accessible to any part of the program via the Pulumi config object.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way.
Some Pulumi providers use the open-source Terraform schemas to determine available resources, parameters, and return/response attributes.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to the cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi is a declarative tool that uses imperative languages to define the end state; the language is used for authoring the program and not for talking to the cloud provider API.
Pulumi uses strongly typed languages that support IntelliSense and the Language Server Protocol, so users rarely need to leave their IDE when defining Pulumi programs.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in, enabled explicitly with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`.
Pulumi experimental features are not necessarily supported and can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
`PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true` is an environment variable that enables Pulumi experimental features.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Pulumi-maintained provider major versions older than the latest (other than the previous major for covered widely used providers) receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Major provider versions typically include significant changes such as deprecations, new resources and new functionality, which may require additional migration steps.
Minor provider versions typically include new resources and features, performance improvements, and bug fixes without introducing breaking changes.
In npm, the tilde operator (e.g. ~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Provider patch versions are primarily for bug fixes and security updates and are designed to be fully backward compatible.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi recommends never being 2 major provider versions behind.
The Provider support policy page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/.
Pulumi ESC FAQ, Pulumi Cloud FAQ, and Pulumi Policies FAQ pages exist at /docs/support/faq/secrets-config/, /docs/support/faq/pulumi-cloud/, and /docs/support/faq/policies/.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The Pulumi Registry has package pages at /registry/packages/aws/, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault for the covered providers.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship security patches.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer versions of language runtimes.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at, unless otherwise prompted via security fixes.
Under the Pulumi provider support policy, exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When major version N+1 of a Pulumi provider ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life on the same day regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the provider LTS major version, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases, but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning a Pulumi provider to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is the recommended approach.
At any time exactly one major version of a covered provider is the LTS version, and older majors receive no patches.
N is the latest released major version: if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) of a Pulumi provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
Pulumi provider versions N-2 and older are end of life, not supported, and receive no updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ page at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'what are the best practices for maintaining provider versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
